thread:
maria: Heads-up — saw repeated throttle spikes in eu-west last night tied to cooldowns + burst pools filling. 503s climbed from ~0.2% -> 1.8% between 23:30-01:00 UTC. Anyone oncall?
ashok: I'm on it, pulling kube/node logs and network metrics now. Is this the same pattern as last month's night spike?
maria: Pattern similar but root looks different — network egress saturation on nodegroup inference-eu-2 triggered kube-probe flaps. Autoscaler reacted, then we had oscillation because reserve buckets were quickly drained.
oliver: That makes sense. Our current policy allows burst up to 60% over reserved, with 5m scale-down cooldown. Short cooldown + burst exhaustion = thrash. I vote we increase scale-down cooldown and add hysteresis.
kevin: Cost note: increasing cooldown/window will raise steady-state GPU hours during peak by ~3-5% based on last week's profile. But reducing retries/throttles also reduces request cost. Might be net-neutral.
lisa: Could be a routing fallback too — have eu-west fall back to eu-central when net egress error rate > 1% for 2m. Smart routing exists but thresholds are conservative atm.
maria: We tried simple fallback earlier and hit quality mismatches (model variant differences). Idea: fallback to same model but a quantized variant (lower perf cost) to keep semantics.
ashok: Quick probe: KV-cache hit-rate dropped ~14% at 23:44 which aligns with cold restarts. That amplified token compute and made burst buckets burn faster.
oliver: Proposal: harmonize SLOs + throttling by (1) bumping burst_holdback to 20m, (2) scale-down cooldown -> 20m, (3) add scale-down hysteresis requiring 2 consecutive low-util windows, (4) add kvcache-hit alert.
kevin: Sounds reasonable. Want to see the config diff and the expected cost delta. If cost delta <3% for the maintenance window and throttles drop to <0.5%, accept.
maria: Draft autoscaler snippet to canary (yaml):
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: AutoscalerPolicy
metadata:
  name: eu-west-harmonize-2026-03
spec:
  reservedCapacityPct: 100
  burstMaxPct: 160  # allow 60% burst
  burstHoldbackMinutes: 20
  scaleDownCooldownMinutes: 20
  scaleDownHysteresisWindows: 2
  prewarmOnScaleUp: true
  quantizedFallback: true  # enable fallback to Q4 variant when routing tripped
```
ashok: I'll wire the kvcache-hit alert: `kvcache.hit_rate < 85% for 3m` and add a dashboard panel for per-node egress throughput.
devops-bot: Deploy queued: autoscaler policy change 'eu-west/harmonize-20m' -> canary rollout 10% at 08:00 UTC. (CI/CD: #4821)
lisa: Quick ask — can we throttle ingress at the edge earlier to avoid filling internal queues? Even simple token-bucket backpressure on the gateway could drop load before it hits autoscaler churn.
oliver: Good idea. We can set soft-ingress-throttle to 120r/s per shard for eu-west during the window. That plus canary should smooth things.
kevin: OK agree next steps: canary deploy, monitor throttles, kvcache, cost impact (72h). If throttles <0.5% and cost delta <2.5% keep; else rollback.
maria: Thanks. I'll own postmortem if we fail criteria. Will post results after 72h monitoring. :thumbsup:
